edge.title: The fine that arrives as a link
edge.setup: An SMS or WhatsApp message says a traffic challan is pending on your vehicle, with a small amount and a link or an app file to 'pay now before it doubles'. The vehicle number may be correct, the page looks official, and the deadline is tonight.
edge.tell: A fine that comes with a link, an app to install, and a deadline of hours.
move: Do not tap the link or install any file sent in the message, even if the vehicle number is correct.
Check for challans yourself: type echallan.parivahan.gov.in into the browser, or use the traffic police's own app, and search by your vehicle number.
If you paid or entered card or UPI details, call your bank at once to block the card, then report on 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in.
edge.why: Vehicle numbers are visible to everyone, so a correct number proves nothing. The message borrows the authority of the traffic police and the fear of a growing penalty so you act before checking. A real fine can be looked up on the official site without any link from a stranger.
edge.variants: Same shape: 'FASTag KYC expired', 'electricity connection will be cut tonight', 'RC or licence suspended, click to update', any pending-dues message with an APK attached.

lens.name: Sunk cost
lens.one_line: Money and time already spent are gone, and should carry zero weight in what you do next.
lens.detail: Rationally, only future costs and benefits matter. Psychologically, abandoning something feels like converting an investment into a loss, so people escalate — another year in the wrong job, another ₹50,000 into a failing car, another two hours of a bad film. The trick that works: ask what you'd advise someone who'd just arrived at this exact situation with no history.
elsewhere: Government projects continued because of money already spent.
Relationships extended by their length rather than their state.
Reading a book to the end because you're halfway.
lens.test: If I were arriving at this fresh today, with nothing already invested, would I choose it?
lens.today: Bengaluru has reworked its mobility plan six years on, but ThePrint reports that big-ticket projects may limit its options, and Namma Metro Phase 3 has just had a third land acquisition notification for the Orange Line package (The Hindu). Money and years already committed are the pull to keep going; the useful question for any civic project is what the remaining cost buys, not what has been spent.

moved.what: Karnataka has issued a third land acquisition notification for the Orange Line package of Namma Metro Phase 3 (The Hindu).
moved.so_what: If you own or rent along the Phase 3 corridor, check whether your survey number appears and read the notification's dates for objections.

moved.what: The inaugural Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat sleeper run is likely on 1 November (Times of India).
moved.so_what: If you need Mumbai that week, watch IRCTC for the booking window before the first fares fill.

moved.what: Farmer groups have called a statewide protest on 23 October (Times of India).
moved.so_what: Check your route on Friday before leaving, especially intercity, and keep a buffer for delays.

moved.what: Indian shares slipped on elevated crude while demand for Jio's IPO was strong (Reuters).
moved.so_what: Elevated crude is how fuel and flight costs reach you later; if you apply to the IPO, use only your own broker or UPI app, and treat any 'guaranteed allotment' message as the scam.

carry_over.prompt: A seller offers gold below market, with a sacred story and a reason it must stay quiet: what is the tell?
carry_over.answer: A price below market, with a story that explains why it must be quick and secret.
